target_customer: Waste and recycling operators, starting with organic waste facilities
problem: Removing contaminants from messy, changing organic waste streams is manual and difficult to automate.
business_model: Robotic systems sold to waste operators (hardware; pricing not published)
product_category: Learning based robotic manipulation for waste sorting

founders.name: Jonas Gruetter
founders.background_notes: Robotics researcher with an ICRA publication per the YC page. Education not listed.

founders.name: Stanislaw Piasecki
education: ETH Zurich, MS in Computational Science and Engineering
founders.background_notes: Earlier projects include autonomous interceptor drones and autonomous race cars.

competitors.name: AMP Robotics
competitors.what: AI robotic sorting, now trialing organics contaminant removal
competitors.traction_then: San Antonio organics site found organics sorting less predictable than recycling (film plastics, moisture)

competitors.name: Recycleye
competitors.what: Computer vision and robotic sorting for material recovery facilities

technical_complexity.rationale: Grasping deformable, contaminated organic waste with learned manipulation and custom hardware is research grade; AMP itself reports organics are fundamentally harder than traditional recycling.

defensibility.rationale: Grasp success and failure data from real facilities could compound, but established sorters have deployments.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found as of the record date.

market_need_then: Operators struggle with contamination in organics and manual sorting; AMP is pairing organics sorting with biochar, signaling market interest.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline: Redefining the economics of waste; a brain that learns the stream

brand_strength.rationale: No brand press found beyond YC launch listings.

outcome_analysis: Grip is a Summer 2026 YC robotics startup with no outcome yet. Two ETH linked robotics engineers target organic waste sorting, a harder niche than standard recycling where AMP reports unpredictable results. Success will depend on grasp reliability in real facilities.
notes: Funding unverified: Dealroom lists a $125k seed and one profile says $500K from Y Combinator; both are aggregators and do not reconcile. Company site offered little content. Competitor details are from trade pages and CB Insights snippets.
